papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning and computational approaches can be used to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal pediatric brain cancer driven by histone H3 alterations and epigenetic dysregulation. It highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics are transforming the study of tumor heterogeneity and treatment resistance, and discusses computational strategies to integrate these data for predicting therapy outcomes.

papers.title: DUET-seq: An Open-Source Droplet Platform for High-Fidelity Joint Chromatin and Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Temporal Regulatory Decoupling in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: Joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell enables direct linkage of regulatory elements to transcriptional output, but existing approaches remain limited by low co-capture sensitivity, proprietary platforms, and high costs. Here we present DUET-seq, an open-source droplet microfluidic platform for joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same nucleus. DUET-seq combines programmable dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads with one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to physically co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments, completin
papers.summary: DUET-seq is an open-source droplet microfluidic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same single nucleus using dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads and one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR. The method improves co-capture sensitivity over existing approaches and reveals temporal decoupling between regulatory element accessibility and transcriptional output in single cells.

papers.title: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Genetic Screening Protocol and Registry: The PERCVD Trial in the Gulf South.
papers.abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a pregnancy-associated form of systolic heart failure with high prevalence and mortality worldwide. It occurs in 1:1800 to 1:3500 births in the United States and disproportionately affects women in the Gulf South. Louisiana has the highest maternal mortality rate in the United States, yet no prospective registry exists to investigate the genetic basis of perinatal cardiovascular disorders, creating an urgent need for genetic assessment.
papers.summary: This paper describes the design of the PERCVD trial, a prospective genetic screening protocol and registry for peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) in the Gulf South region of the United States. It aims to address the lack of genetic data on PPCM in a population with disproportionately high maternal mortality, particularly in Louisiana.

papers.title: Association of PRKCB Polymorphisms with Non-syndromic Orofacial Cleft among a Chinese Population.
papers.abstract: To investigate the association of PRKCB polymorphisms with non-syndromic orofacial cleft (NSOC) among a Chinese population.
papers.journal: The Chinese journal of dental research
papers.summary: This study investigates whether genetic variants in the PRKCB gene are associated with non-syndromic orofacial cleft (NSOC) in a Chinese population. The authors analyze PRKCB polymorphisms to assess their potential role in cleft susceptibility, contributing to understanding the genetic basis of this common birth defect.

papers.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic and medicinal-chemistry evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, making tumors more susceptible to immune attack. The authors also discuss generative bioorganic frameworks for designing next-generation combination agents.

papers.title: Predicting Oncogenic Mutants of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Lung Cancer by Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a frequently mutated protein kinase found in patients suffering from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although therapeutic drugs targeting EGFR are available, not all patients respond to these drugs, and it is not yet known whether some clinically detected mutations are actionable. Although the oncogenicity of some mutants is well established, many mutants found in patients are not yet classified or classified as Variants of Uncertain Significance. For newly discovered rare mutants, strong evidence supporting their classification into oncogenic
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with machine learning to predict whether EGFR mutations found in lung cancer patients are oncogenic. The approach aims to help classify Variants of Uncertain Significance, which currently complicate treatment decisions for non-small cell lung cancer. By modeling mutation effects on protein dynamics and learning patterns from known mutants, the method offers a potential computational tool for prioritizing actionable mutations.

papers.title: Machine Learning Guided Discovery of Microbiome Metabolites That Inhibit HDAC.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase (HDAC) is a family of key epigenetic regulator implicated in inflammation, metabolism, and cancer. Microbiome metabolites can modulate host histone acetylation, yet systematic identification of metabolites that target HDAC remains limited. Here we present a computationally driven discovery pipeline that combines training data composition optimization with experimental validation to prioritize microbiome-derived HDAC inhibitors. Starting from a large, public HDAC3 screening data set (314,129 compounds; 485 actives), we developed an automated iterative sampling strategy that
papers.summary: This study presents a machine learning pipeline that combines training data optimization with experimental validation to identify microbiome-derived metabolites that inhibit HDAC enzymes. Starting from a large public HDAC3 screening dataset, the authors developed an iterative sampling strategy to prioritize candidate microbiome metabolites as potential epigenetic modulators relevant to inflammation, metabolism, and cancer.

papers.title: Functional Annotation of Alzheimer's Disease-Associated SNPs Based on Three-Dimensional Chromatin Structure.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have identified numerous loci associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the effector genes and regulatory mechanisms underlying many of these associations remain unresolved. This challenge is particularly pronounced for non-coding variants, whose regulatory effects may extend over long genomic distances and cannot be reliably inferred from the nearest gene alone. Here, we developed an integrative computational framework that incorporates three-dimensional chromatin interactions, expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL), and sequence-level regulatory
papers.summary: This study presents a computational framework that links Alzheimer's disease-associated non-coding GWAS variants to their target genes by integrating 3D chromatin interaction data with eQTL and sequence-level regulatory annotations. The approach addresses the challenge that non-coding risk variants often regulate genes far away, making nearest-gene assignments unreliable. It provides a more accurate functional annotation of AD risk loci.

papers.title: Integrative Proteomics and Genome-Scale Modeling Elucidate Metabolic Flux Shifts in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CC-4414 Under Light Stress.
papers.abstract: The green microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii holds substantial promise as a photosynthetic cell factory for sustainable bioproduction, yet strain-specific metabolic responses to environmental stress remain underexplored. Here, we reconstructed a genome-scale metabolic network (GSMN) of the light-tolerant strain C. reinhardtii CC-4414 by combining de novo genome assembly with integrative proteomics. The resulting model, designated iYH2021, comprises 2021 genes, 2601 reactions, and 2089 metabolites, representing the first genome-scale metabolic reconstruction reported for this strain. To elucid
papers.summary: This study reconstructed the first genome-scale metabolic model for the light-tolerant Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-4414 by combining de novo genome assembly with proteomics data. The model, iYH2021, captures 2021 genes, 2601 reactions, and 2089 metabolites, and was used to analyze metabolic flux shifts under light stress. It provides a strain-specific resource for understanding and engineering stress-tolerant microalgae for bioproduction.

papers.title: Allele-Specific MicroRNA-Binding Variants at Colorectal Cancer Risk Loci in a Hispanic/Latino Population: An Integrative GWAS, All of Us, and Epigenomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) disproportionately affects Hispanic individuals, who remain underrepresented in genomic discovery and lack ancestry-matched functional resources. Many CRC risk variants are non-coding, and those in 3' untranslated regions (3' UTRs) can alter microRNA (miRNA) binding sites and reprogram post-transcriptional gene regulation. Here, we identify allele-specific miRNA-binding variants at CRC risk loci within the Hispanic population using a discovery pipeline anchored to Hispanic-relevant resources. CRC-associated 3' UTR variants were compiled from the GWAS Catalog, further ve
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study identifies genetic variants in the 3' UTRs of genes at colorectal cancer risk loci that alter microRNA binding sites, using a pipeline anchored to Hispanic/Latino-specific resources including GWAS data, All of Us, and epigenomic datasets. The work addresses the underrepresentation of Hispanic individuals in genomic research and highlights how ancestry-matched functional annotation can reveal population-specific regulatory mechanisms in CRC.

papers.title: SMORE: joint dimension reduction and cell population discovery on single-cell methylome data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling technology captures novel epigenetic data modality but are challenging to analyze because of their heterogeneity, high dimensionality, and ultra-sparsity. Here we present SMORE (Single-cell MethylOme Reduction and Embedding), a computational method for joint dimensionality reduction and cell population discovery dedicated to single cell DNA methylation data. SMORE operates on a Bayesian framework that converts methylation proportions into ordered methylation states and jointly infers a low-dimensional representation, cell populations and their number. By u
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SMORE is a new computational method for analyzing single-cell DNA methylation data, which is notoriously sparse and high-dimensional. It uses a Bayesian framework to simultaneously reduce dimensionality, identify cell populations, and determine the number of populations, converting methylation proportions into ordered states. This addresses a key bottleneck in the emerging field of single-cell epigenomics.

papers.title: Exploring the association between gastroesophageal reflux disease and hyperlipidemia through bioinformatics and Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: Observational research has found a relationship between gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and hyperlipidemia (HLP). This study explored the relationship between GERD and HLP using bioinformatics and Mendelian randomization (MR) methods. We first conducted bioinformatics analyses to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from disease datasets and then performed a two-sample MR analysis with aggregated genome-wide association study (GWAS) data to investigate the relationship. 11 DEGs were shared between GERD and HLP. According to the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) en
papers.summary: This study combined bioinformatics (differential gene expression analysis) with two-sample Mendelian randomization using GWAS data to investigate whether gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is causally linked to hyperlipidemia. The authors identified 11 shared differentially expressed genes between the two conditions and applied MR to assess a potential causal relationship. The work aims to clarify whether the observed observational association reflects causation or shared genetic architecture.

papers.title: HisTrader identifies nucleosome-free regions within ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications.
papers.abstract: Enhancers and promoters regulate cell identity through the binding of transcription factors (TFs) to specific DNA motifs within accessible chromatin. These regulatory regions are often identified using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-based assays targeting histone modifications, such as ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq), HiChIP, and proximity-ligation-assisted ChIP-seq (PLAC-seq). However, the large size of the enriched regions, or peaks, can make it difficult to pinpoint the precise DNA sequence where TFs act or where trait- or disease-associated variants exert their effects. We present HisTrad
papers.summary: HisTrader is a computational method that pinpoints nucleosome-free regions within large histone modification ChIP peaks (from ChIP-seq, HiChIP, PLAC-seq) to more precisely localize transcription factor binding sites and regulatory variants. This improves the resolution of enhancer and promoter mapping beyond standard peak calling.

papers.title: Using Brain Organoids to Explore Human Neurobiology.
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges in neuroscience is understanding how the human brain develops into a highly organized and functionally integrated organ, because many developmental processes cannot be investigated directly in humans and are not fully recapitulated in animal models. Brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells have emerged as powerful three-dimensional (3D) experimental models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, including regional patterning, cellular diversification, and neural circuit assembly. Recent advances in long-term organoid culture, organ
papers.summary: This review discusses how brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells serve as 3D models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, such as regional patterning, cellular diversification, and neural circuit assembly. It highlights recent advances in long-term organoid culture that enable more faithful study of human brain biology where animal models fall short.

papers.title: Hybrid CNN and multi-head attention model for analyzing epigenetic mechanisms and gene expression across fungal phylogenetic distances.
papers.abstract: Understanding gene expression is crucial for optimizing biological processes in bioeconomic processes, human health, and environmental regulation. Epigenetic modifications significantly influence gene expression by altering chromatin structure and DNA accessibility. However, knowledge about the conservation of these mechanisms across species, especially in non-model organisms, is limited. This study predicts gene expression levels based on epigenetic modifications across fungal species, facilitating knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less understood species. We developed a deep lear
papers.summary: The authors developed a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks and multi-head attention to predict gene expression levels from epigenetic modifications across fungal species. The model enables knowledge transfer from well-characterized fungi to less-studied species, helping reveal how epigenetic mechanisms are conserved across phylogenetic distances.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Cardiovascular Genetics: From Multimodal Diagnosis to Risk Prediction and Precision Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a bridge between high-dimensional cardiovascular phenotyping and genomic interpretation in children with inherited and congenital heart disease. This review focuses specifically on where AI-assisted approaches in pediatric cardiovascular genetics have progressed beyond proof-of-concept, how the maturity of evidence differs between general genomic tools and pediatric cardiovascular applications, and what is required for responsible clinical translation. Inherited and rare cardiovascular disorders are characterized by genetic heterog
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being used to connect detailed cardiovascular imaging and clinical data with genomic information in children with inherited and congenital heart disease. It highlights where AI approaches have moved beyond early proof-of-concept, contrasts the maturity of general genomic tools with pediatric cardiovascular applications, and outlines what is needed for responsible clinical translation.

papers.title: "Updates on diagnostic and prognostic molecular biomarkers of CNS tumors".
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors has undergone a paradigm shift over the past decade, evolving from a purely histology-based approach to an integrated framework that incorporates molecular and epigenetic features. This review summarizes recent updates in key genomic and epigenomic biomarkers across major CNS tumor categories, with a focus on their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. DNA methylation profiling has emerged as a valuable tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, complementing traditional histopathologic assess
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in molecular and epigenetic biomarkers used to diagnose and classify central nervous system tumors, highlighting the shift from purely histology-based diagnosis to an integrated molecular framework. It emphasizes DNA methylation profiling as a key tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, alongside other genomic biomarkers with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Transcriptome-based epigenetic screening identifies DNA hypermethylation signatures as prognostic biomarkers in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Promoter DNA hypermethylation is a key epigenetic mechanism of gene silencing in cancer, yet the DNA hypermethylome of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and its prognostic relevance remain poorly characterized. Here, we systematically identified and validated novel hypermethylated genes with prognostic significance in OSCC using a genome-wide discovery and multi-platform validation strategy. Candidate genes were first identified by pharmacologic demethylation combined with RNA sequencing across OSCC cell lines, then validated by quantitative RT-PCR, methylation-specific PCR, and bisulfite se
papers.summary: This study used pharmacologic demethylation combined with RNA sequencing to identify genes silenced by promoter DNA hypermethylation in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cell lines. Candidate hypermethylated genes were validated across multiple platforms and shown to have prognostic significance, suggesting DNA methylation signatures could serve as biomarkers for OSCC.

papers.title: Phage Genomics and Bioinformatics in Therapeutic Development: Evidence Limits, Validation Gates, and Translational Decision-Making.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial resistance has renewed interest in live therapeutic phages, including engineered candidates and defined phage cocktails, as antibacterial strategies. However, clinical translation requires evidence extending beyond phage isolation and computational prediction. This review examines how phage genomics and bioinformatics can support phage-based antibacterial development while remaining aligned with pharmaceutical requirements for safety, quality, pharmacology, and clinical validation. Methods: This narrative review synthesizes the literature on the generation,
papers.summary: This review discusses how phage genomics and bioinformatics can support the development of phage-based antibacterial therapies, emphasizing that computational predictions and phage isolation alone are insufficient for clinical translation. It outlines the evidence limits, validation gates, and translational decision-making needed to meet pharmaceutical standards for safety, quality, pharmacology, and clinical validation.

papers.title: The Plant Cell Wall: From Structural Diversity and Biosynthesis to Integrity Signaling and Physiological Functions.
papers.abstract: Plant cell walls are dynamic structural matrices that provide mechanical support while regulating growth, transport, environmental sensing, and defense. Their properties emerge from the coordinated biosynthesis, deposition, assembly, and remodeling of cellulose, hemicelluloses, pectins, lignin, and specialized wall polymers, yet how wall architecture is coupled to integrity surveillance and whole-plant physiology remains incompletely understood. Here, we synthesize current knowledge of plant cell wall classification, major polymer biosynthesis and assembly, cell wall integrity signaling, and p
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on plant cell wall composition, biosynthesis, and assembly, covering cellulose, hemicelluloses, pectins, and lignin. It also examines how cell wall integrity signaling connects wall architecture to whole-plant physiology, growth, and defense. The paper highlights gaps in understanding how wall structure is coupled to surveillance mechanisms and physiological outcomes.

papers.title: FetchPA: a guided, end-to-end solution for local ATAC-Seq data processing and analyses.
papers.abstract: Local genome accessibility strongly correlates with activity of cis-regulatory elements, and Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin coupled with next-generation sequencing (ATAC-Seq) has emerged as method of choice to profile chromatin accessibility in both healthy and pathogenic conditions. The introduction of streamlined protocols and manufacturer kits has made this technique accessible to labs of a variety of disciplines, background, and research interests. Many bioinformatics tools have been created for the quality control, mapping, and visualization of ATAC-seq data, however these too
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FetchPA is a guided, end-to-end software solution that streamlines local processing and analysis of ATAC-Seq data, addressing the fragmentation of existing bioinformatics tools. It aims to make chromatin accessibility profiling accessible to labs with limited computational expertise by integrating quality control, mapping, and visualization steps into a single workflow.

papers.title: The Epigenetic Aging-Cancer Continuum: Biomarkers, Metabolism, and Therapy.
papers.abstract: Aging and cancer form a biological continuum influenced by epigenomic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, cellular senescence, and loss of tissue homeostasis. Age-related epigenetic alterations can promote cancer, which exploits plasticity for evolution, immune evasion, metastasis, and resistance. Nutrition and metabolism affect this process through one-carbon metabolism, methyl-donor availability, acetyl-CoA and NAD+ balance, redox status, microbiome metabolites, and chromatin enzyme activity. Circulating biomarkers such as cell-free DNA methylation, mutation-based ctDNA, fragmentom
papers.summary: This review argues that aging and cancer are not separate processes but a continuum driven by epigenetic changes, metabolic dysfunction, and inflammation. It highlights how nutrition and metabolism influence this continuum through one-carbon metabolism, methyl donors, acetyl-CoA/NAD+ balance, and microbiome metabolites, and discusses circulating biomarkers like cell-free DNA methylation and ctDNA for tracking it.

papers.title: Flow Orchestrated Regulatory Genomics Engine (FORGE): A Configurable Nextflow Pipeline for End-to-End snMultiome Analysis.
papers.abstract: Single-nucleus resolution multiome (snMultiome) assays concurrently profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same nucleus. Yet regulatory inference from such analyses are difficult to scale, audit, and reproduce; moreover, as a field, snMultiomics and its' toolset remains far from standardized. To address these challenges we developed FORGE, a configureable Nextflow workflow that carries paired data from raw counts and fragments through regulatory network inference with a comprehensive differential testing suite. Execution is containerized, tracks provenance, robust to interr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FORGE is a configurable Nextflow pipeline that automates end-to-end single-nucleus multiome analysis, taking paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility data from raw counts through regulatory network inference and differential testing. It addresses the lack of standardization in snMultiome workflows by providing a containerized, provenance-tracking, and reproducible solution.

papers.title: A comprehensive map of the bovine mobilome and their epigenetic regulation of mastitis.
papers.abstract: Retrotransposons are major components of mammalian genomes, yet their genome-wide annotation and epigenetic regulation in cattle remain incompletely characterized. Here, we present a comprehensive annotation and integrative epigenomic analysis of major retrotransposon classes in the bovine genome, with emphasis on DNA methylation patterns and their potential roles in subclinical mastitis. Using a multi-step de novo pipeline, we identified and classified long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs), short interspersed nuclear elements (SINEs), and endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) in the bovine refe
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive genome-wide annotation of retrotransposons (LINEs, SINEs, and ERVs) in the bovine genome using a de novo multi-step pipeline, and integrates this with epigenomic data on DNA methylation. The authors link retrotransposon methylation patterns to subclinical mastitis, suggesting these mobile elements may play regulatory roles in the disease. The work expands the catalog of bovine repetitive elements and their epigenetic regulation.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the CBL Gene Family in Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa.
papers.abstract: Calcineurin B-like (CBL) protein-mediated calcium signaling represents a core regulatory pathway underlying plant abiotic stress adaptation. Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa (sour jujube) is a perennial woody species with remarkable saline-alkali and drought tolerance, yet the CBL gene family in this species has not been systematically characterized.
papers.summary: This study systematically identifies and characterizes the CBL (calcineurin B-like) gene family in sour jujube, a woody species known for its tolerance to saline-alkali and drought stress. The authors provide a genome-wide inventory of these calcium-signaling genes, laying groundwork for understanding how this species adapts to harsh environments.

papers.title: Genetic Variants Involved in Metformin Pharmacokinetics in the Chilean Population.
papers.abstract: To estimate the frequency and potential impact of genetic variants involved in metformin pharmacokinetics, including gastrointestinal absorption, renal elimination, and hepatic transport in the Chilean population.
papers.summary: This study examines the frequency of genetic variants affecting metformin pharmacokinetics—covering gastrointestinal absorption, renal elimination, and hepatic transport—in the Chilean population. It aims to assess how these variants might influence metformin response and dosing in this specific population.

papers.title: The Exposome-Brain Axis: A Scoping Review of Biological Biomarkers in Environmental Neurotoxicity, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: The escalating global burden of neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders is deeply intertwined with cumulative environmental toxicant exposure. To accurately capture the prodromal and subclinical impacts of this multi-chemical "pollutome", research is shifting from symptom-based assessments toward the use of objective, quantifiable biological indicators. Guided by the PRISMA-ScR framework, this scoping review systematically analyzed literature across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase databases without temporal restrictions. The final selection included 52 human observational s
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 52 human observational studies examining biological biomarkers that link cumulative environmental toxicant exposure (the 'exposome') to neurotoxicity, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. It highlights a shift from symptom-based assessments toward objective, quantifiable biomarkers for capturing prodromal and subclinical neurological impacts of multi-chemical exposures.

papers.title: H3K27me3 Drives Constricted Migration-Induced 3D Genome Rewiring in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Repeated exposure of neoplastic cells to mechanical stresses during metastasis can drive stable morphological and physiological changes. We previously showed that A375 human melanoma cells subjected to 10 rounds of constricted migration ("Bottom-10 cells") became significantly more migratory and exhibited H3K9me3 relocalization, transcriptional remodeling, and chromatin compartment changes relative to naïve parental A375 cells. Because these phenotypes persist across cell divisions, we hypothesized they are driven and maintained by specific epigenetic mechanisms. We profiled candidate histone
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how repeated mechanical stress from constricted migration causes lasting changes in melanoma cells. The authors find that the histone modification H3K27me3 drives rewiring of the 3D genome organization in these cells, linking mechanical forces during metastasis to stable epigenetic and transcriptional changes.

papers.title: Deep phenotyping of EHMT1 ankyrin repeat domain missense variants in Kleefstra syndrome by multi-tiered structural genomics analyses at atomic resolution.
papers.abstract: EHMT1 is a lysine methyltransferase that writes and reads histone methylation marks to repress transcription. Deleterious mutations in EHMT1 cause Kleefstra syndrome (KLEFS1; OMIM #610253), a congenital neurodevelopmental disorder. Many of these affect the ankyrin repeat (ANKR) domain, which recognizes histone H3 lysine-9 methylation and mediates interactions with other epigenetic regulators. However, the functional consequences of EHMT1 missense variants within the ANKR domain remain poorly characterized, as nearly 50% are currently classified as variants of unknown significance (VUS). To add
papers.summary: This study uses multi-tiered structural genomics analyses at atomic resolution to functionally characterize missense variants in the ankyrin repeat domain of EHMT1, which cause Kleefstra syndrome. The work aims to resolve the ~50% of such variants currently classified as variants of unknown significance by linking structural perturbations to functional consequences. It provides a framework for deep phenotyping of disease variants in epigenetic regulators.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Prioritization of Candidate Drug Targets in Tumors Using Spatial Multi-Omics.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is reflected in cell composition, molecular states, spatial distribution, and microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics can map in situ expression and cell states but cannot fully explain upstream regulation, while spatial epigenomics provides complementary evidence such as chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation. This review summarizes the applications of spatial multi-omics and deep learning in prioritizing candidate drug targets in tumors.
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial multi-omics technologies (combining spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics) can capture tumor heterogeneity across cell composition, molecular states, and microenvironment interactions. It highlights how deep learning methods can integrate these complementary spatial data layers to prioritize candidate drug targets in tumors.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological covariates on single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses of epigenetic variation.

papers.title: Synergistic role of molecular imaging and genomics in thyroid cancer management: from diagnosis to personalized treatment.
papers.abstract: The management of thyroid cancer has advanced through the integration of molecular imaging, genomic profiling, and bioinformatics, supporting precision oncology across diverse subtypes. Although radioiodine imaging and therapy remain standard for differentiated thyroid cancers, efficacy can be limited in refractory cases due to heterogeneous iodine uptake. Advances including dosimetry-guided radioiodine therapy, hybrid imaging modalities (SPECT/CT, PET/CT, PET/MRI), and novel radiotracers (FDG, NaF) may improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic decision-making, particularly for aggressive tu
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining molecular imaging (such as PET/CT, SPECT/CT, and novel radiotracers) with genomic profiling can improve the diagnosis and personalized treatment of thyroid cancer, especially for aggressive or radioiodine-refractory subtypes. It highlights that integrating imaging and genomic data through bioinformatics supports more precise therapeutic decision-making across diverse thyroid cancer subtypes.

papers.title: Complete Mitochondrial Genome of the Endemic Loach Leptobotia tchangi and Its Phylogenetic Placement Within Botiidae.
papers.abstract: Leptobotia tchangi is a loach species endemic to South China, but its mitochondrial genome has not yet been characterized, limiting understanding of its evolutionary relationships and conservation genetics.
papers.summary: This study sequenced and characterized the complete mitochondrial genome of Leptobotia tchangi, an endemic loach from South China, and used it to infer the species' phylogenetic position within the family Botiidae. The new mitogenome provides a molecular resource for evolutionary and conservation studies of this poorly characterized species.

papers.title: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: The inactivation of tumour suppressor genes is a key step in cancer development, and is usually achieved by homozygous loss. In prostate cancer, however, large genomic regions are often hemizygously lost, which complicates the identification of putative tumour suppressors in these regions. Here, we develop Epi2Hit, an integrative computational method that leverages whole genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling and gene expression to identify biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes involving DNA methylation of promoter and enhancer regions of one allele and genomic loss of the other a
papers.summary: The authors developed Epi2Hit, a computational method that integrates whole-genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling, and gene expression data to detect biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes caused by DNA methylation of one allele combined with genomic loss of the other. Applying this to prostate cancer, they identified recurrent epigenetic silencing events and nominated new putative tumour suppressor genes that would be missed by approaches focused only on homozygous deletion.

papers.title: A patient-derived missense mouse model of Kabuki syndrome 1.
papers.abstract: Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1) is a rare cause of intellectual disability resulting from heterozygous pathogenic variants in the gene encoding the histone methyltransferase KMT2D. A previously established loss-of-function mouse model of KS1 exhibits key phenotypic features, and therapeutic trials in this mouse model suggest postnatal malleability of neurological symptoms. However, 15-30% of individuals with KS1 carry missense variants. To investigate whether missense variants lead to similar phenotypic presentation in mice, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce the KS1- patient variant R5179, corresp
papers.summary: This study uses CRISPR-Cas9 to create a mouse model carrying the patient-derived KMT2D missense variant R5179, which causes Kabuki syndrome type 1. The model allows researchers to study whether missense variants produce similar phenotypes to the previously established loss-of-function model, addressing a gap since 15-30% of KS1 patients have missense mutations.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling Primer: Focus on Chromatin and Epigenetics.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in modern biology is to understand how molecular interactions produce cellular and organismal functions across vast spatiotemporal scales. Nowhere is this challenge more apparent than in the study of chromatin, where meters of DNA compact into a micron-sized nucleus. How this polymer folds is a dynamic process, regulated by epigenetic modifications-chemical changes to DNA and histones that involve only a handful of atoms. These small changes cooperate to produce emergent, higher-order structures that define cellular identity and function. To explain this system, we must int
papers.summary: This primer reviews multiscale modeling approaches for understanding how chromatin folds within the nucleus and how epigenetic modifications regulate this process across scales. It highlights how tiny chemical changes to DNA and histones produce emergent higher-order chromatin structures that define cellular identity and function. The article serves as an introductory guide for integrating molecular, polymer, and cellular-level models of chromatin and epigenetics.

papers.title: Programmable RNA-Guided DNA Recombination: Mechanisms, Engineering, and Applications.
papers.abstract: The emergence of seekRNA- and bridgeRNA-guided recombination has introduced a distinct paradigm in genome engineering by coupling programmable RNA-directed DNA recognition with recombinase-mediated insertion, excision, inversion, and genomic rearrangement without canonical double-strand breaks. Since their discovery in 2024, these systems have progressed rapidly from bacterial mobile genetic elements and mechanistic characterization to structural elucidation and programmable genome engineering in human cells. However, these advances remain distributed across foundational and rapidly emerging s
papers.summary: This review covers seekRNA- and bridgeRNA-guided DNA recombination, a new genome engineering approach that uses programmable RNA to direct recombinases for DNA insertion, excision, and inversion without creating double-strand breaks. It traces the rapid development of these systems from their 2024 discovery in bacterial mobile genetic elements to structural characterization and application in human cells.

papers.title: Cross-Scale Convergence in Epigenetic Gene Regulation: A Perspective on Functional Enrichment Analytics for Cancer.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation of gene expression is studied at three physical scales: micro: DNA sequence-level methylation/demethylation; meso: nucleosome occupancy and remodeling; and macro: chromosomal domain silencing by Polycomb complexes, heterochromatin, and topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries. The challenge to fully understand epigenetic gene regulation patterns is that these scales are not independent. Their influence overlaps and they share a recurring architectural theme across scales of a targeted molecular pattern followed by cooperative, feedback-driven, spatially bounded s
papers.summary: This perspective argues that epigenetic gene regulation operates across three interconnected physical scales—DNA-level methylation, nucleosome occupancy, and higher-order chromosomal domains—and that these scales share a recurring architectural pattern of targeted molecular action followed by cooperative, feedback-driven, spatially bounded responses. The authors propose that functional enrichment analytics must account for this cross-scale convergence to properly interpret epigenetic patterns in cancer.

papers.title: GenoME: a MoE-based generative model for individualized, multimodal prediction and perturbation of genomic profiles.
papers.abstract: The non-coding genome operates through a complex, multiscale regulatory system where regulated gene expressions are closely associated with cell-type-specific histone modifications, transcription factor binding, and 3D conformation. Developing computational models that can integrate these patterns to predict and interpret the regulatory system remains challenging. Here, we present GenoME, a Mixture of Experts (MoE)-based generative model that uses DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq signals to predict a unified genomic profiles encompassing epigenomics, transcriptomics, and chromatin
papers.summary: GenoME is a Mixture-of-Experts generative model that integrates DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq signals to predict unified multimodal genomic profiles spanning epigenomics, transcriptomics, and chromatin conformation. It enables individualized, multimodal prediction and in silico perturbation of regulatory profiles, offering a framework for interpreting the non-coding regulatory system.

papers.title: DNA methylation-based ageing in a deuterostome invertebrate: an epigenetic clock for the crown-of-thorns seastar (Acanthaster cf. solaris).
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable ageing tools are essential for wildlife conservation and management. While DNA methylation has emerged as a promising tool for age estimation in vertebrates, its application to invertebrates remains contested and has been limited to arthropods. Here, we develop an epigenetic clock for the Pacific crown-of-thorns seastar (CoTS; Acanthaster cf. solaris), a destructive coral predator contributing to habitat degradation across Indo-Pacific reefs. Using Oxford Nanopore Technologies, we generated whole-genome DNA methylation profiles across five age groups and identified 1910 C
papers.summary: This study developed the first DNA methylation-based epigenetic clock for an echinoderm, the crown-of-thorns seastar, using Oxford Nanopore whole-genome methylation profiling across five age groups. It identified 1,910 age-associated CpG sites, demonstrating that epigenetic ageing tools can be extended beyond vertebrates and arthropods to deuterostome invertebrates. The clock offers a potential conservation and management tool for this destructive coral predator.

papers.title: A Marine Brevibacillus-Derived Membrane-Lytic Peptide: Molecular Insight and Biophysical Characterization of a Novel AMP, FNL62-AMP.
papers.abstract: This study characterizes the genomic identity, functional efficacy, and computational biophysics of FNL62-AMP, a novel antimicrobial peptide isolated from a phylogenomically distinct, newly identified Brevibacillus species. Production kinetics revealed a late-exponential phase onset of antibacterial activity with sustained potency against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). LC-MS/MS analysis identified the peptide sequence as NH2-LLLLFR-COOH. FNL62-AMP demonstrated excellent formulation resilience, retaining full anti-MRSA activity under high thermal stress (80 °C for 6 h) and
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes FNL62-AMP, a novel antimicrobial peptide from a newly described marine Brevibacillus species, with the sequence LLLLFR. The peptide shows sustained activity against MRSA and remains fully active after extreme heat treatment (80 °C for 6 hours), suggesting good formulation stability. Computational biophysics and genomic analyses provide insight into its membrane-lytic mechanism.

papers.title: Classical Homocystinuria Incidentally Diagnosed Following a Normal Newborn Screening Result.
papers.abstract: Classical homocystinuria (HCY) due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency is included in many newborn screening programs, which traditionally use dried blood spot (DBS) methionine as the primary biomarker. However, some patients have normal or only mildly elevated methionine in the neonatal period, leading to false-negative results. We report a four-month-old male infant referred for sagittal craniosynostosis, whose metabolic evaluation revealed markedly elevated plasma methionine and total homocysteine concentrations. Genetic analysis identified a homozygous, pathogenic variant (c.10
papers.summary: This case report describes a four-month-old infant with classical homocystinuria who had a normal newborn screening result because the standard dried blood spot methionine biomarker can miss cases in the neonatal period. The diagnosis was made incidentally after referral for sagittal craniosynostosis, when metabolic testing revealed markedly elevated methionine and total homocysteine, and genetic testing confirmed a homozygous pathogenic CBS variant. The case highlights a false-negative limitation of methionine-based newborn screening for CBS deficiency.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review examines the two main sequencing strategies used in wastewater-based surveillance of viruses: targeted approaches (amplicon- and probe-based) that sensitively detect known pathogens, and untargeted approaches that can reveal novel viruses. It also highlights common bioinformatic pitfalls in wastewater virome analysis, providing guidance for researchers designing population-level viral monitoring studies.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Structural Characterization of Secondary Metabolite Biosynthetic Gene Clusters in African Baobab (Adansonia digitata).
papers.abstract: Adansonia digitata L., known as the African Baobab, is renowned for its extraordinary longevity and its long-standing use in traditional African medicine. However, the genomic basis underlying its specialized secondary metabolism remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to computationally identify and characterize putative biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) within the publicly available A. digitata genome assembly (GenBank accession GCA_029448705.1) using an integrated bioinformatics pipeline. Ab initio gene structure prediction was performed with AUGUSTUS (Arabidopsis thaliana species mode
papers.summary: This study computationally scanned the publicly available African baobab genome to identify biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) responsible for secondary metabolite production, using an integrated pipeline including AUGUSTUS gene prediction. It provides a first genome-wide catalog of putative BGCs in this long-lived medicinal tree, laying groundwork for understanding its specialized metabolism.

papers.title: Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images.
papers.abstract: The functional decline of the hematopoietic system during aging affects organismal function and contributes to reduced healthspan. Quantifying hematopoietic aging holds great scientific and clinical relevance. Alterations in chromatin architecture are a well-established hallmark of aging that encode rich and informative signatures of the aging process, yet they remain largely unexplored as quantitative markers. Here, we present an interpretable deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks, ChromAgeNet, that learns changes in the spatial features of chromatin architecture upon
papers.summary: The authors developed ChromAgeNet, an interpretable convolutional neural network that predicts hematopoietic stem cell aging from 3D chromatin architecture images. The model learns spatial chromatin features associated with aging, demonstrating that chromatin organization can serve as a quantitative marker of the aging process. This offers a new deep learning-based approach for assessing hematopoietic aging with potential scientific and clinical relevance.

papers.title: Investigation of allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids reveals the association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation and high expression in citrus genomes.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation plays a central role in the regulation of gene expression. In plants, methylation occurs in the CG, CHG, and CHH contexts, via distinct DNA methyltransferases including MET1, CMT3, and the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway via DRM2. In interspecific hybrids, these epigenetic mechanisms are confronted to a mixed small RNA population and two subgenomes harbouring specific methylation patterns, therefore generating unique expression profiles. The aim of this work was to understand these regulations by analysing gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNAs in a citrus
papers.summary: This study examines allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids to understand how epigenetic regulation differs between subgenomes. It finds that small RNA-mediated de novo methylation (via the RdDM pathway) is associated with high gene expression in citrus genomes, contrary to the typical repressive role of methylation. The work links siRNA-directed methylation patterns to expression differences in interspecific hybrids.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study analyzed DNA methylation patterns in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) patients to identify differentially methylated regions linking environmental exposures to disease onset. The findings highlight involvement of Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks, suggesting epigenetic mechanisms mediate the interplay between viral exposure and genetic susceptibility in early MS pathogenesis.

papers.title: ChoCallate: a computational pipeline for consensus germline variant calling in genomic sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Accurate germline variant calling in non-model and polyploid organisms remains challenging due to sequencing errors, genomic complexity, and caller-specific biases. Existing ensemble methods of variant calling are constrained by species-specific training, limited portability, or an inability to process multiple samples concurrently. To address these limitations we developed ChoCallate, a Nextflow-based pipeline for consensus germline variant calling. The pipeline integrates three species-independent callers, bcftools, FreeBayes, and Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) HaplotypeCaller, within a flex
papers.summary: ChoCallate is a Nextflow-based pipeline that combines three species-independent variant callers (bcftools, FreeBayes, and GATK HaplotypeCaller) to generate consensus germline variant calls. It is designed to handle non-model and polyploid organisms, where existing ensemble methods struggle due to species-specific training requirements or limited scalability. The pipeline supports concurrent processing of multiple samples, improving portability and accuracy for challenging genomes.

papers.title: The causal integration ladder: a multilevel evidence framework for therapeutic target evaluation in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Cervical-cancer genomic studies nominate many altered genes, but the evidence needed to distinguish disease association from a causal, therapeutically tractable mechanism is rarely stated explicitly. We present the Causal Integration Ladder (CIL), an evidence-accounting framework that distinguishes Level I association, inherited Level II-G evidence, acquired Level II-S evidence, Level III computational and direct functional evidence, and Level IV translational validation, while treating viral etiology as an explicit context modifier. An exploratory TCGA-CESC screen (306 tumours, 3 normal sampl
papers.summary: The authors propose the Causal Integration Ladder (CIL), a framework for organizing and grading the strength of evidence linking genomic alterations in cervical cancer to causal, therapeutically actionable mechanisms. The framework distinguishes association-level evidence from inherited, acquired, functional, and translational validation tiers, while explicitly accounting for viral etiology as a context modifier. An exploratory TCGA-CESC screen illustrates the approach.

papers.title: TattleTail: A Rule-Based Tool for Identifying Canonical Pyocin-Encoding Gene Clusters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Tailocins are phage tail-like bacteriocins derived from prophages that have lost the ability to package viral genomes while retaining bactericidal activity against related bacterial strains. In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, these elements are referred to as pyocins and contribute to ecological fitness and antimicrobial applications. Despite lacking essential phage components, pyocin-encoding gene clusters share substantial sequence homology with phage tail genes, creating a major challenge for genome annotation. Current prophage prediction tools, which rely on phage gene homology, can frequently mis
papers.summary: TattleTail is a new rule-based computational tool designed to identify canonical pyocin-encoding gene clusters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes. It addresses the problem that existing prophage prediction tools misclassify pyocins as prophages due to their shared sequence homology with phage tail genes. The tool provides a more accurate way to annotate these bactericidal elements, which are important for bacterial ecology and potential antimicrobial applications.

papers.title: Challenges in the detection and assembly of virus integration structures in human genomes.
papers.abstract: Oncogenic viral infections are major contributors to cancer development worldwide. Tumor-associated viruses such as human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) can promote malignant transformation through diverse mechanisms, including persistent viral gene expression, chronic inflammation, and, in some cases, integration of viral DNA into the host genome. Among these, HPV is one of the most clinically important DNA tumor viruses and is a major driver of cancers of the cervix, anus, penis, vagina, vulva, and oropharynx, col
papers.summary: This review examines the technical challenges of detecting and assembling viral integration structures within human genomes, focusing on oncogenic viruses such as HPV, HBV, EBV, and MCPyV. It highlights how viral DNA integration contributes to cancer development and discusses the computational and methodological obstacles in accurately identifying these integration events from sequencing data.

papers.title: Interpreting antimicrobial resistance from bacterial whole-genome sequencing: prediction tools, database fragmentation, analytical trade-offs, and harmonized reporting.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has become a critical component of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance because it can characterize bacterial lineages, resistance determinants, and, when sequence resolution is sufficient, the mobile genetic elements that mediate dissemination. However, the practical value of WGS-based AMR inference remains constrained by fragmentation across AMR databases, inconsistent nomenclature, variable curation practices, and differences in analytical thresholds and reporting rules. Consequently, the same isolate may yield discordant resistome outputs across tools,
papers.summary: This review examines how whole-genome sequencing is used to infer antimicrobial resistance in bacteria, highlighting that practical value is limited by fragmented AMR databases, inconsistent nomenclature, variable curation, and differing analytical thresholds. The authors argue that these issues cause the same isolate to produce discordant resistome results across prediction tools, and they call for harmonized reporting standards.

papers.title: Extensively Drug-Resistant ST16 Klebsiella pneumoniae Co-Harboring bla KPC-2, bla OXA-181, and Chromosomal bla NDM-4: Genomic Features and Therapeutic Challenges.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) represents a major global public health threat due to its high-level antimicrobial resistance and limited therapeutic options. The emergence of CRKP isolates co-harboring multiple carbapenemase genes further complicates clinical management and infection control. This study aimed to characterize the antimicrobial resistance phenotype, complete genomic features, and carbapenemase gene environments of an extensively drug-resistant ST16 CRKP bloodstream isolate co-harboring class A, B, and D carbapenemases.
papers.summary: This study characterizes an extensively drug-resistant ST16 Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream isolate that simultaneously carries three different carbapenemase genes (blaKPC-2, blaOXA-181, and chromosomal blaNDM-4). The authors use phenotypic and complete genomic analyses to describe the resistance profile and the genetic environments surrounding these carbapenemase genes, highlighting the therapeutic challenges posed by such multi-carbapenemase isolates.

papers.title: A methodological framework for real-world performance studies of clinical variant classification platforms at early organizational stages.
papers.abstract: Automated platforms that classify sequence variants under the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework are increasingly used in rare-disease genomics, yet methodology for characterizing their performance at an early organizational stage is underdeveloped. The two framings most common in the literature are poorly suited to this stage: single-source comparison treats one peer laboratory or curated set as ground truth, which is difficult to defend at evidence depths where qualified laboratories disagree 25%-35% of the time; and for
papers.summary: This paper proposes a methodological framework for evaluating automated ACMG/AMP variant classification platforms during early organizational adoption, when traditional single-source comparisons are unreliable because expert laboratories disagree on 25-35% of variants. It argues for performance studies designed around real-world evidence depths rather than treating any single curated set as ground truth.

papers.title: Association and Mechanistic Insights Linking Bisphenol A to Psoriasis: Integrative Analysis of Bulk Transcriptomics, Network Toxicology, Mendelian Randomization and Single‑cell RNA Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated skin disease with complex etiology, and environmental factors such as bisphenol A (BPA) exposure are suspected pathogenic factors. This study aimed to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers linking BPA exposure to psoriasis and to explore the latent interaction and mechanisms between BPA and candidate biomarkers.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, network toxicology, Mendelian randomization, and single-cell RNA sequencing to investigate whether bisphenol A (BPA) exposure contributes to psoriasis. The authors identify candidate diagnostic biomarkers that link BPA exposure to psoriasis and propose potential mechanistic pathways underlying this environmental-immune interaction.

papers.title: Integrated genomic analysis of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia: resistome, virulence-associated genes, predicted mobile genetic elements, and core-genome phylogeny.
papers.abstract: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an emerging opportunistic pathogen characterized by intrinsic multidrug resistance and broad ecological distribution. However, its genomic characteristics across publicly available clinical, environmental, and animal isolates remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study performs an integrated genomic analysis of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates from clinical, environmental, and animal sources, characterizing their resistome, virulence-associated genes, and mobile genetic elements. It also reconstructs a core-genome phylogeny to assess the population structure and evolutionary relationships among these isolates. The work provides a broader genomic perspective on this emerging multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen.

papers.title: Residual based anomaly detection framework for variant caller dispatch in DNA sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Reliable and scalable variant analysis is an enabling component of genomic studies involving microbial communities, host-associated microorganisms, and their hosts, and may support future investigations of genetic heterogeneity within symbiotic systems. Widely used workflows incorporating BWA and GATK provide standardized default processing routes, but their performance may vary across genomic regions containing repetitive sequences, complex structures, or atypical local sequence characteristics. Applying a context-aware software-recommendation procedure to every genomic region, however, can s
papers.summary: This paper proposes a residual-based anomaly detection framework to dynamically dispatch different variant callers to different genomic regions in DNA sequencing data. The approach aims to improve variant calling accuracy in challenging regions with repeats or complex structures, which is particularly relevant for microbial and host-associated microbiome studies. It addresses the limitation of using a single default caller like GATK across heterogeneous genomic contexts.

papers.title: In silico transcriptomic analysis nominates TSPAN32 as a central node of SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming in intestinal epithelial cells.
papers.abstract: Microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) regulate intestinal epithelial homeostasis and immune tolerance. Yet, the specific host effector genes that mediate these responses remain poorly defined, limiting the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) analysis of transcriptomic data to identify host genes that respond to microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in intestinal epithelial cells. The authors nominate TSPAN32 as a central hub gene in the SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming of these cells. The work is purely computational and proposes TSPAN32 as a candidate biomarker or therapeutic target, though experimental validation is not provided.

papers.title: From sequence to timescale: a frequency-domain control-theoretic framework linking ncRNA sequence composition to epigenetic regulatory timescales.
papers.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are central regulators of epigenomic states, orchestrating chromatin modifications, gene silencing, and nuclear architecture through recruitment of chromatin-modifying complexes. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) such as XIST, HOTAIR, and MALAT1 exemplify these regulatory roles. Despite their importance, quantitative computational frameworks for linking ncRNA sequence composition to temporal regulatory behaviour remain limited. We introduce a frequency-domain control theory framework modelling RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, extending a previously established s
papers.summary: The authors propose a frequency-domain control-theoretic framework that models non-coding RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, aiming to link sequence composition to the timescales of epigenetic regulation. This extends prior work by providing a quantitative computational approach to relate ncRNA sequence features to temporal regulatory dynamics.
